goal: Build hello-loop, a tiny bookmarks service on the Python standard library: a SQLite table for bookmarks, a JSON API to add and list them, and a server-rendered page that shows them and lets a visitor add one. Local only; no deployment, no authentication.

items.title: Bookmarks schema, migration and seed
items.intent: Add the bookmarks table as the first migration (with its down migration) and a seed command that loads three sample bookmarks. Everything else reads and writes this table.
acceptance: AC-F1-1: after `python3 -m hello_loop.migrate` on a fresh database, table `bookmarks` exists with columns `id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), `url` (TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE), `title` (TEXT NOT NULL) and `created_at` (TEXT NOT NULL), and nothing else
AC-F1-2: running `python3 -m hello_loop.migrate` a second time succeeds and `schema_migrations` holds `0001_create_bookmarks` exactly once
AC-F1-3: `python3 -m hello_loop.migrate --down` removes the `bookmarks` table and its `schema_migrations` row (this is the item's down migration)
AC-F1-4: `python3 -m hello_loop.seed` inserts exactly 3 sample bookmarks; running it twice still leaves exactly 3 rows
AC-F1-5: `tests/test_schema.py` exists, covers AC-F1-1 to AC-F1-4, and passes under `verify_tests`

items.title: Bookmarks JSON API
items.intent: Expose bookmarks over HTTP: create one, list all (newest first), fetch one by id. Input is validated; a duplicate url is a conflict. Responses are JSON.
acceptance: AC-F2-1: `POST /api/bookmarks` with JSON `{"url": "https://example.com/", "title": "Example"}` returns 201 and a JSON object with `id`, `url`, `title` and `created_at` (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`)
AC-F2-2: `GET /api/bookmarks` returns 200 and `{"bookmarks": [...]}` ordered newest first (highest id first)

AC-F2-3: `POST /api/bookmarks` returns 400 and `{"error": "<message>"}`, and stores nothing, when the body is not a JSON object, `url` is missing or does not start with `http://` or `https://`, or `title` is missing or blank after trimming
AC-F2-4: `POST /api/bookmarks` with a url that is already stored returns 409 and `{"error": "<message>"}`, and adds no row
AC-F2-5: `GET /api/bookmarks/<id>` returns 200 and the object for an existing id, and 404 with `{"error": "<message>"}` for an unknown or non-numeric id
AC-F2-6: `tests/test_bookmarks_api.py` exists, covers AC-F2-1 to AC-F2-5 against the running server, and passes under `verify_tests`; demo target `GET /api/bookmarks` returns 200 under `verify_run`

items.title: Bookmarks page
items.intent: A server-rendered page at / that lists the bookmarks as links and has a form to add one. It reuses the API's validation and data access, and must escape everything a visitor typed.
acceptance: AC-F3-1: `GET /` returns 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`; each bookmark appears as `TITLE`, newest first
AC-F3-2: with no bookmarks the page contains the text `No bookmarks yet.`
AC-F3-3: a bookmark whose title is `<script>alert(1)</script>` is rendered as `<script>alert(1)</script>`, and the page contains no raw `<script>` tag; `&` in a url is rendered as `&`

AC-F3-4: the page contains `<form method="post" action="/bookmarks">` with inputs named `url` and `title`; posting valid form data (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) returns 303 with `Location: /` and stores the bookmark; invalid data returns 400 with an HTML page that shows the validation message, and stores nothing
AC-F3-5: `tests/test_page.py` exists, covers AC-F3-1 to AC-F3-4, and passes under `verify_tests`; demo target `GET /` returns 200 under `verify_run`
